# **Exercise 1**

```{r chunk-11,, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Step 1: Install and load necessary packages (if not installed, run install.packages(c("readr", "dplyr", "ggplot2", "ggrepel")) first)
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(ggrepel) # For smart label placement

# Step 2: Read CSV data
data <- read_csv("pisa_2022.csv")

# Step 3: Group by country and calculate average math and reading scores
avg_scores <- data %>%
group_by(country) %>%
summarise(
avg_math = mean(math, na.rm = TRUE), # na.rm = TRUE handles possible missing values
avg_read = mean(read, na.rm = TRUE)
)

# Step 4: Draw a scatter plot (AUS points are red, others are black; labels are placed intelligently using ggrepel)
ggplot(avg_scores, aes(x = avg_math, y = avg_read)) +
geom_point(data = subset(avg_scores, country != "AUS"), # Other points: black
color = "black", size = 2, alpha = 0.8) +
geom_point(data = subset(avg_scores, country == "AUS"), # AUS points: red, stand out
color = "red", size = 3, alpha = 0.9) + # Slightly larger for emphasis
geom_text_repel( # Smart labeling using ggrepel
aes(label = country),
size = 3, # Label font size
box.padding = 0.5, # Label spacing
point.padding = 0.3, # Spacing between point and label
max.overlaps = 10, # If you modify: Limit overlapping labels to a maximum of 10
segment.color = "grey50", # Connector color
segment.size = 0.2 # Connector thickness
) +
labs(
title = "Average Mathematics and Reading Scores of Students Across Countries (AUS Highlighted)",
x = "Mean Scores in Mathematics",
y = "Mean Scores in Reading"
) +
theme_minimal() # Use a minimalist theme


```

```{r chunk-12,, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
# Load necessary packages
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(tidyr)
library(cowplot) # Used to merge charts and extract legends

# Step 1: Read CSV data (for your complete data set of 80 countries)
data <- read.csv("pisa_2022.csv")

# Step 2: Calculate mean scores for each country and gender
mean_scores <- data %>%
group_by(country, gender) %>%
summarise(
math_mean = mean(math),
read_mean = mean(read),
science_mean = mean(science),
.groups = 'drop'
)

# Step 3: Calculate diff = female_mean - male_mean
wide_data <- mean_scores %>%
pivot_wider(names_from = gender, values_from = c(math_mean, read_mean, science_mean))

# Check column names (for debugging, can be deleted)
#print("Wide format data column names:")
#print(colnames(wide_data))

diff_data <- wide_data %>%

mutate(
math_diff = math_mean_female - math_mean_male,
read_diff = read_mean_female - read_mean_male,
science_diff = science_mean_female - science_mean_male
) %>%

select(country, math_diff, read_diff, science_diff) %>%

# Convert country to a factor and sort alphabetically

mutate(country = factor(country, levels = unique(country[order(country)])))

# Output diff values ​​(optional, for inspection)
#print("Gender differences in subjects for each country (female - male):")
#print(diff_data)

# Step 4: Draw a scatter plot for each subject (add Boys/Girls labels + zero reference line)
# Math scatter plot (left, showing Y axis)
p_math <- ggplot(diff_data, aes(x = math_diff, y = country, color = math_diff > 0)) +
geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.5) + # Zero reference line
annotate("text", x = -max(abs(diff_data$math_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Boys",
hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + # Boys label (left)
annotate("text", x = max(abs(diff_data$math_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Girls",
hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + # Girls label (right)
scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "blue", "FALSE" = "red"),
) +
labs(title = "mean_math",
x = "diff", y = "country",
color = "diff > 0") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8), # Y-axis font
legend.position = "none") + # Hide the legend for this plot (will be extracted later)
NULL

# Read the scatter plot (center, hide the Y axis)
p_read <- ggplot(diff_data, aes(x = read_diff, y = country, color = read_diff > 0)) + 
geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) + 
geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.5) + 
annotate("text", x = -max(abs(diff_data$read_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Boys", 
hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + 
annotate("text", x = max(abs(diff_data$read_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Girls", 
hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + 
scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "blue", "FALSE" = "red"), ) +
labs(title = "mean_read",
x = "diff", y = NULL, # Hide Y title
color = NULL) +
theme_minimal() +
theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), # Hide Y scale
axis.title.y = element_blank(),
legend.position = "none") +
NULL

# Science scatter plot (right side, hide Y axis)
p_science <- ggplot(diff_data, aes(x = science_diff, y = country, color = science_diff > 0)) +
geom_point(size = 2, alpha = 0.7) +
geom_vline(xintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", color = "black", size = 0.5) +
annotate("text", x = -max(abs(diff_data$science_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Boys", 
hjust = 0, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + 
annotate("text", x = max(abs(diff_data$science_diff))*0.3, y = Inf, label = "Girls", 
hjust = 1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2, color = "gray50") + 
scale_color_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "blue", "FALSE" = "red"), 
) + 
labs(title = "mean_sci", 
x = "diff", y = NULL, 
color = NULL) + 
theme_minimal() + 
theme(axis.text.y = element_blank(), 
axis.title.y = element_blank(), 
legend.position = "none") + 
NULL

# Step 5: Extract the unified legend (from p_math)
legend <- get_legend(p_math + theme(legend.position = "right")) # Extract and move to the right

# Remove the legend from p_math (redefine the legendless version)
p_math_no_legend <- p_math + theme(legend.position = "none")

# Merge three plots (horizontally, with a shared Y axis)
combined_plots <- plot_grid(p_math_no_legend, p_read, p_science,
ncol = 3, nrow = 1, align = "h",
rel_widths = c(1, 1, 1), # Equal widths
labels = c("A", "B", "C"),
label_x = 0.02, label_y = 0.98)

# Add the legend to the right
combined_plot <- plot_grid(combined_plots, legend,
ncol = 2, nrow = 1, rel_widths = c(3, 0.5)) # Plot:Legend = 3:0.5

# Display the combined plot
print(combined_plot)


```

# **Exercise 2**

```{r}

# Load necessary packages
library(ggplot2)

# Read the CSV file, skipping the first 10 rows of metadata
data <- read.csv("aus_median_house_price.csv", skip = 10, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# View the data structure (optional, for debugging)
# head(data)
# str(data)

# The first column is the time (date), converted to a standard date format (assuming quarterly end, e.g., Mar-2002 is converted to 2002-03-31)
data$Date <- as.Date(paste0(data[,1], "-01"), format = "%b-%Y-%d")
# More precise quarterly conversion: map Mar-2002 to 2002-03-31, Jun-2002 to 2002-06-30, etc.
months <- c("Mar" = "03-31", "Jun" = "06-30", "Sep" = "09-30", "Dec" = "12-31")
data$Date <- as.Date(paste0(substring(data[,1], 5, 8), "-", months[substring(data[,1], 1, 3)],
substring(data[,1], 1, 3)), format = "%Y-%m-%d")

# Extract Melbourne median house price (4th column)
melbourne_prices <- data[, 4] # Assuming the 4th column is Melbourne prices, based on the CSV structure
melbourne_df <- data.frame(Date = data$Date, Price = as.numeric(melbourne_prices))

# Remove NA values(if there are empty data)
melbourne_df <- na.omit(melbourne_df)

# Draw a line chart
ggplot(melbourne_df, aes(x = Date, y = Price)) +
geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
geom_point(color = "red", size = 0.5) + # Add points to highlight data points
labs(title = "Median Price Trend for Existing Houses in Melbourne",
x = "Time (Quarterly)",
y = "Median Price ($'000)") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)) # Rotate the x-axis labels to avoid overlap




```

```{r}
# Load necessary packages
library(ggplot2)
library(lubridate)

# Read the house CSV file, skipping the first 10 rows of metadata
house_data <- read.csv("aus_median_house_price.csv", skip = 10, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Parse the house date ("Mar-2002" → 2002-03-31)
months <- c("Mar" = "03-31", "Jun" = "06-30", "Sep" = "09-30", "Dec" = "12-31")
house_data$Date <- as.Date(paste0(substring(house_data[,1], 5, 8), "-", months[substring(house_data[,1], 1, 3)]))

# Extract Melbourne median house price (column 4)
melbourne_df <- data.frame(Date = house_data$Date, Price = as.numeric(house_data[, 4]))
melbourne_df <- na.omit(melbourne_df) # Remove NA

# Read GDP CSV
gdp_data <- read.csv("aus_GDP_changes.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# Parse GDP date ("1/1/2002" → 2002-03-31; parts[1] is fixed "1", parts[2] is quarter code "1/4/7/10")
gdp_data$Date <- NA
for (i in 1:nrow(gdp_data)) {
date_str <- gdp_data$DATE[i]
parts <- strsplit(date_str, "/")[[1]] 
if (length(parts) == 3) { 
qmonth <- parts[2] 
year <- parts[3] 
month_end <- switch(qmonth, "1" = "03-31", "4" = "06-30", "7" = "09-30", "10" = "12-31") 
if (!is.null(month_end)) { 
gdp_data$Date[i] <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-", month_end)) 
} 
}
}
gdp_data$Date <- as.Date(gdp_data$Date)
gdp_data <- gdp_data[!is.na(gdp_data$Date), ] # Remove invalid dates
gdp_data$GDP_changes <- as.numeric(gdp_data$GDP_changes) # Convert to numeric values
gdp_data <- na.omit(gdp_data) # Remove NAs

# Filter housing data for the time period (2002-03-31 to 2025-06-30)
start_date <- as.Date("2002-03-31")
end_date <- as.Date("2025-06-30")
gdp_filtered <- gdp_data[gdp_data$Date >= start_date & gdp_data$Date <= end_date, ]

# Identify periods of low growth (<0.1%)
low_gdp <- gdp_filtered[gdp_filtered$GDP_changes < 0.1, ]

# Add a new variable to the housing data: low_gdp (TRUE if low growth occurred in that quarter)
melbourne_df$low_gdp <- melbourne_df$Date %in% low_gdp$Date

# Create a shadow rectangle data frame (for each low growth quarter: xmin = quarter start, xmax = quarter end)
shadow_df <- data.frame(
xmin = floor_date(low_gdp$Date, "quarter"),
xmax = ceiling_date(low_gdp$Date, "quarter") - days(1), # day before quarter end
ymin = min(melbourne_df$Price) - 50, # price range buffer
ymax = max(melbourne_df$Price) + 50
)

# Draw a line chart + shadow
p <- ggplot(melbourne_df, aes(x = Date, y = Price)) +
geom_rect(data = shadow_df, aes(xmin = xmin, xmax = xmax, ymin = ymin, ymax = ymax),
fill = "red", alpha = 0.2, inherit.aes = FALSE) + # Shaded area
geom_line(color = "blue", size = 1) +
geom_point(color = "red", size = 0.5) +
labs(title = "Trend in Melbourne's median price of existing homes (shaded: GDP growth <0.1%)",
x = "Time (quarterly)",
y = "Median price ($'000)") +
theme_minimal() +
theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 14),
axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))

# Show the plot
print(p)

# See an example of the new variable (optional debugging)
# head(melbourne_df)

```
